svg.text: enrollStudent — three guards, then two writes, all under ONE lock
Course "Java 101" · maxCapacity = 3 · already holds ENR-1 (s-1), ENR-2 (s-2), ENR-3 (s-3)
GUARD 2 is this student ALREADY active on this course ?
walks only THIS student's enrolments — O(k), thanks to the secondary index ✓
a DROPPED enrolment does not block a re-enrol, which is the behaviour you want
= 3, and maxCapacity = 3 ⇒ s-4 EXITS HERE: "Course C-JAVA is at full capacity (3)"
this scans EVERY enrolment on the platform — O(E), the one real hot spot here
COMMIT two map writes, no rollback needed
both writes happen inside the same lock, so no reader ever sees one without the other ✓

g.text: THE RACE THIS LOCK EXISTS TO STOP — and the one it does not
Guard 3 reads a count and then writes. Without the lock, two threads can both count 2 seats used
against a capacity of 3, both pass, and both enrol — 4 students in a 3-seat course. ConcurrentHashMap
cannot save you here: each individual operation is atomic, the SEQUENCE is not. That is check-then-act,
and it is the single most common concurrency bug an interviewer will probe for.
Right instinct: put the lock around the whole compound operation, keep the pure reads lock-free.
Wrong granularity though: it is `synchronized` on the SERVICE, so every enrolment on the platform
queues behind every other, even for unrelated courses.
Fix: a per-course lock (a striped lock keyed on courseId), or better — hold an AtomicInteger seatsTaken on
Course and CAS it. Then capacity is O(1) instead of O(E), and the check-then-act disappears entirely.

svg.text: THE MAPS, AFTER THREE SUCCESSFUL ENROLMENTS
lessonProgress is keyed by STUDENT then LESSON, not by enrolment ⇒ progress survives a drop-and-re-enrol ✓
…and that is also the bug: nothing ties a completed lesson back to a course, so completeLesson can
record a lesson for a student who was never enrolled, and it still returns true.
PROGRESS — a fold over the COURSE's lessons, not the student's map
Driving the fold from the COURSE's lesson list is what makes it correct: adding L6 tomorrow
re-bases every student to 3/6 automatically. Counting the student's own map would not. ✓
Unknown course or student ⇒ returns 0.0, indistinguishable from "enrolled but nothing done".
No weighting by lesson duration, no partial video progress, no "last watched position".
ASSESSMENT — the part that is honestly not implemented
The submitted answers are never read. Quiz is a one-field stub with no questions, so there is
nothing to grade against. The AssessmentResult is returned and then never stored.
In an interview: name it as a stub, then fix it aloud — Quiz holds List<Question> with a correctIndex,
grading is a zip-and-count, and results append to an attempts map so "best of 3" becomes possible.
EnrollmentStatus — the state machine the enum promises
progress hitting 100% should flip it to COMPLETED;
an unenrol should flip it to DROPPED — neither exists
the duplicate-enrol guard already READS the status,
so the machine is half-built: consumed, never advanced
easy win: enum-driven transitions + guarded setters
Say this out loud: "the enum declares four states but only ACTIVE is reachable — the transitions are the
first thing I would add, because every downstream feature (certificates, refunds, seat reclaim) depends on them."
Legend: green = implemented & defensible · grey dashed = declared but unreachable · red = honest gap · orange = the hot spot
